messages.content: is i run home yesterday right?
use i ran home yesterday. ran is used for that past sentence.
now make it about my brother every day.
my brother runs home every day.
what if he is doing it now?
my brother is running home now.
why running after is?
is running puts the running at this moment. runs every day is about something he does often.
now ask whether he did it yesterday.
did my brother run home yesterday?
can you know he was tired after running?
no. running home does not tell us for sure how he felt after.
only give what we do not know about that.
we do not know how he felt after running.
only give the first past sentence again.
i ran home yesterday.
write a longer story about two pages that look similar. a child should need more than color to find the one she wants.

a child wanted the page where she had written a short story. she remembered that it was on blue paper, so she asked her brother to bring the blue page from the table. he came back with a drawing on another blue page. she had not kept in mind that they had used the same color for both. instead of saying he had not listened, she explained that her page had words at the top and no drawing. he looked again and found it under a book. she read the first line to check, then said thank you. the color had helped begin the request, but it had not been enough to choose one page from all the things on the table.
why did he bring a drawing first?
it was also on a blue page, and she had only asked by color.
what detail helped him find the story?
she said it had words at the top and no drawing.
can you know the drawing was his?
no. the story gives what was on the page, not who made it.
write the more clear request.
please bring the blue page with words at the top, not the blue drawing.
finish with her reading the right page.
she opened the page at the table and read the story while he looked for his own book.
i got an answer to my question, but now i have a new question.
that can happen when an answer helps you see another part you want to understand.
does it mean the first answer did not help?
not always. it may have helped enough for you to ask something more specific.
i first asked where the book was. now i know it is on the shelf, but i want to know whose it is.
those are different questions. the place answer does not tell you who has the book as their own.
can you ask the new question simply?
whose book is on the shelf?
why not ask where again?
because you already have the place you needed. now you want a different kind of information.
what if the book moved after i got the answer?
then you may need to ask where it is now. the old place answer may no longer be true.
make that explanation shorter.
if it moved, the place question is open again.
only give the question about whose book it is again.
whose book is on the shelf?
what is different about another book and the other book?
another book can be one more or a different book. the other book usually is a specific one left from a pair or group.
make that explanation shorter.
another can be new or different. the other usually is known from context.
there are two books. i have one, and i want the one i do not have. what can i say?
please bring me the other book.
what if there are many books and i just want a different one?
please bring me another book.
does another always mean i keep the first one too?
not always. it can mean one more, or a different one instead. context helps make that clear.
make it clear i want to return this one and get a different one.
i would like to return this book and choose another one.
only give the question asking for the specific one from two.
could you bring me the other book?
write a longer story about someone returning a book to the house but not yet to the person who needs it. that detail should change a simple reading plan.

a boy told his sister that he had brought her book back. she went to the table where she usually read and could not find it. he explained that the book was at home, inside a container by the front door. she had thought back was about putting it in the place where she needed it. they found the book together and put it on the table before the reading time. next time, he said the place when telling her it was back. she could then choose whether to get it herself or ask him to bring it the rest of the way. the first message had not been a lie, but it had left out a detail important to her task.
what did he mean by back?
he was talking about the book being in the house again.
make that answer shorter.
the book was back at home.
what had his sister thought?
she thought it would be on the table where she read.
make that answer shorter.
she thought back was about the reading table.
write a more clear message from the boy.
your book is back at home. it is in the container by the front door.
finish with the reading place ready.
they put the book on the table, moved a cup out of the way, and sat down to read.
give me a request with sit.
please sit near the window.
now say i did it yesterday.
i sat near the window yesterday.
can sitting be about now?
yes. i am sitting near the window now.
what if i only write a person sitting near a window under a picture?
it can give what is in the picture, though it is not the same as saying i am sitting there now.
make that explanation shorter.
it can be about a picture, not about where you are now.
now make it a full sentence about a made up person.
a woman is sitting near the window.
can you know it is my room?
no. the example does not give that detail.
only give the yesterday sentence again.
i sat near the window yesterday.
i wrote the wrong time in one line of a message. the rest is right. help me explain that.
i gave the wrong time in one line. the rest of the message is still correct.
now add the old and new time. i wrote four but mean five.
i wrote four, but the correct time is five. the rest of the message is still correct.
can i only send five with no explanation?
you can, but the other person may not know what it changes. saying four should be five makes clear which detail changed.
make that explanation shorter.
give the old time and the new time so the change is clear.
now give that as a short message.
the time should be five, not four. the rest is still correct.
does this mean i have to send the whole message again?
not always. if that short change is clear, it may be enough.
only give the changed time sentence.
the time should be five, not four.
write a longer story about a person saying about five minutes and a child hearing it as a sure five. use simple words for the difference.

a child asked how long his father needed before leaving. his father said about five minutes. the child watched the clock and stood up as soon as five minutes had gone. his father still had one line to finish on a page. the child said the time was over. his father explained that about had made the number a general idea, not a sure answer for the last moment. the child asked him to say whether they should wait by the door or keep reading. they chose to keep their books open until he called. the number had helped, but the word about was part of the answer too.
why was the child ready to leave after five minutes?
he heard the number as a sure time without using the word about.
what could he ask to make the waiting useful?
should we wait by the door, or do we have time to keep reading?
make the difference between about five and a sure five clear.
about five minutes is a general idea of the time, not a sure answer for the last moment.
can you write a more specific answer if the father knows he needs one more minute?
i need one more minute, then i will be ready.
finish with the child closing the book when called.
he kept reading until his father called. then he put the book away and went to the door.
i know all the words in this list, but i want to learn to use them in different sentences.
we can try changing the order, the time, or who is doing the thing, while keeping the meaning clear.
use read, book, and sister in a sentence.
my sister reads a book.
now make it yesterday.
my sister read a book yesterday.
now make it a question asking whether she did that.
did my sister read a book yesterday?
why can the same words help make different sentences?
the order and the helping words change what the sentence does. it can tell, ask, or say something did not happen.
make that explanation shorter.
the order can change a sentence from telling something to asking about it.
now say she did not read yesterday.
my sister did not read a book yesterday.
only give the first sentence again.
my sister reads a book.
i plan to read on three days and draw on one more day if i have time. how many days are sure in that plan?
three reading days are the sure part you gave. drawing is another day only if you have time.
make that answer shorter.
three days are sure. drawing is still open.
what is the important detail for the drawing day?
whether you have enough time.
only give the plan about reading now.
you plan three reading days.
if i do have time, how many different days is that?
four different days, because you said one more day for drawing.
what if i draw on one of the reading days instead?
then it can be three different days. that changes the first plan, which gave drawing another day.
make that explanation shorter.
then it is three days instead of four.
only give the answer for one more day.
four days.
write a longer story about two books with a different price. a child should learn that price alone does not tell which book will help with the question they have.

a child wanted a book about plants. at the shop, one book had a price of five coins and many pages. another had a price of three coins and more pictures. he first thought the one for five coins must be the right book for him. his mother asked what he wanted to learn. he said he wanted to start with simple words and see what each part of a plant looked like. they opened both books and looked at a page. the one with more pictures answered his first questions more clearly. he chose it for that reason, not from price alone. the other book might help him later when he wanted more detail. the choice came from what he wanted to learn now.
what did price alone not tell him?
it did not tell which book would help with the question he had now.
what helped him choose?
he looked at the words and pictures in both books and used his learning goal.
make that answer a full sentence with price in it.
the price did not tell him which book would help with the question he had now.
was the longer book wrong for everyone?
no. it might help someone who wanted more detail, or help him later.
finish with him using the book at home.
he opened the book at his desk and used the first picture to ask a new question about the plant.
my friend said thanks for helping. give me a short reply without another question.
you are welcome. it is good that it helped.
make that reply shorter.
you are welcome.
now just two words.
no problem.
now give me a short goodbye instead.
take care.
only goodbye now.
goodbye.
